methods.name: testPersonalOpenWaitsForForegroundAndRecordsOncePerMount
covers: Real controller initially has no window: accepted read and explicit activation call cannot write.
Attach the same controller to a foreground scene, call the actual current lifecycle method, record the first open.
A native read/version refresh and repeated activation calls retain the same mount/attempt identity.
After original unmount/drain and another actual mounted owner, record exactly one additional local date.
limits: The test container suppresses automatic appearance forwarding so automatic load cannot mask the explicit-hook regression.
This is controlled window visibility and direct lifecycle-hook coverage; it does not drive UIApplication background/foreground or the SwiftUI notification publisher.

methods.name: testPersonalOpenRejectsRetiredReadAndCancellationBeforeDispatch
covers: Complete old HTTP read held through existing delivery seam; new mounted owner accepts different actual source bytes first.
Late old completion cannot replace current editor bytes or cause a local write.
Cancel current observation while its real definition request is held before bound dispatch; release and join with zero effects.
A later mounted open records exactly one local date.

methods.name: testPersonalOpenRetainsLateAcknowledgmentAndDrainsBeforeReopen
covers: Native-shaped bound success and synchronous ACK precede failing readback plus outer session postflight; existing accepted-but-unverified message proves retained ACK classification.
No automatic retry after clearing only the controlled verifier fault and refreshing the document.
Separately hold an old post-ACK lease noncooperatively, retire/remount, accept new read, then release old task and observe the next bound mutation after the release.
Retired completion cannot publish warning/clear the new owner's task; final original drain joins all work.
Before releasing the held predecessor, await the exact newer owner's first-lease entry as an inverted one-second observation; premature progress fails and later positive entry is required.
limits: The second flow records actual event ordering for this controlled schedule; it is not an executed mutation-testing or exhaustive scheduler claim.
The first flow proves the UI ACK classification; the store's private attempt UUID ledger is not introspected or fabricated.
